page.desc: A 3-in-1 MagSafe stand draws 25 + 5 + 5 = 35 W and a Qi2 car charger needs 35 W in. Three one-cart kits, sized so each charger gets its full 25W.
page.answer: Short answer. An Apple MagSafe charger needs a 30W adapter for 25W, but a full home and car setup needs more: a 3-in-1 stand draws 25 + 5 + 5 = 35 W and a Qi2 car charger wants 35 W input. Best kit: ESR's 3-in-1 + OmniLock car bundle, whose parts ship with 50 W and 40 W adapters.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Home stand: 25 W to the phone + 5 W to the Watch + 5 W to the AirPods = 35 W. That is more than the 30 W adapter Apple names for its single puck. ESR's 50 W charger leaves 50 − 35 = 15 W of headroom before conversion losses.
  • Car: the OmniLock needs at least 35 W in before it tries Qi2.2 speed. The included adapter's USB-C port gives 40 W, so 40 − 35 = 5 W is spare. Its 18 W USB-A port is 35 − 18 = 17 W short.
  • Single puck: UGREEN's MagFlow Pro asks for 45 W. The Nexode 65W's USB-C ports give 65 W, so 65 − 45 = 20 W is spare. Its USB-A port gives 22.5 W, half of what the puck needs, so use a USB-C port.
  • Bundle saving: on 2026-11-11, $109.99 + $62.99 = $172.98 bought separately at ESR, against $149.13 for the bundle, a $23.85 saving. Adding the car charger costs $149.13 − $109.99 = $39.14 over the stand alone.
  • Speed ceiling: all three kits top out at 25 W. That full rate reaches iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max. iPhone 16 and 16 Pro peak at 22.5 W, iPhone Air at 20 W, and iPhone 17e or iPhone 15 and older at 15 W (Apple). MacRumors reported that the iPhone 16 family needs iOS 26 for 25 W from third-party Qi2.2 chargers.
Your setupPickWhy

If you charge an iPhone, an Apple Watch and AirPods at the bedside and also want the phone charging on the road, pick the bundle: {kit:kit-esr-home-car-bundle}. Both power supplies are sized above what the chargers draw, and the car half costs $39.14 more than the stand alone.

If the car isn't part of the plan, or your vents are round or bladeless, buy the stand on its own: {kit:kit-esr-3-in-1-nightstand}. It charges the same three devices from its own 50 W charger.

If you only charge the phone, this is the classic one-puck setup with a supply that meets the puck's 45 W requirement and still has a second USB-C port free: {kit:kit-ugreen-puck-65w}.

How much power a MagSafe setup really needs

Apple's rule covers one charger and one phone: a 30W (15V/2.0A) USB-C adapter for up to 25 W, a 20W adapter for up to 15 W, and 12 W at minimum, which charges more slowly. A setup adds loads on top of that, and each end of it has its own power source:

ChargerWhat it needsSource
Apple MagSafe Charger, 25 W30 W or greater adapter (15V/2.0A)Apple Support
ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 (25 W + 5 W + 5 W)35 W of output; ships with a 50 W chargerMacworld (Simon Jary)
ESR OmniLock car charger35 W minimum input; included adapter gives 40 W on USB-C9to5Mac (Bradley Chambers)
UGREEN MagFlow Pro puck45 W adapter required, sold separatelyUGREEN
UGREEN MagFlow Pro 2-in-1 and 3-in-145 W+ input for 25 WUGREEN

In the car, Bradley Chambers of 9to5Mac wrote that a USB-A port built into the car, "or even a USB-C port, is probably not going to provide enough power" for Qi2.2 speed. The charger still works from those ports, but slower. Plug it into the 40 W USB-C port on the included 12 V adapter. At home, Macworld's Simon Jary measured an iPhone 16 Pro going from 0% to 50% in just over half an hour on the ESR 3-in-1 with its own charger. Both ESR pieces need a magnetic case 2 mm or thinner.

Not recommended

ESR's 15W road-trip bundle (Magnetic Wireless Car Charger 15W + 25W CryoBoost Foldable 3-in-1, $121.58 on 2026-11-11). It costs $149.13 − $121.58 = $27.55 less than the 25 W bundle. But its car charger tops out at 15 W, and ESR's listing says an "18W QC adapter required for fast charging (not included)". You pay for the cheaper bundle, then still have to buy a car adapter. Also avoid powering any 25 W car mount from the car's own USB port, and running Apple's puck on a 20W adapter, which caps it at 15 W.
